covers: chunk replace, truncate, or delete (size, mtime_ns, or inode change) — admission falls back to SHA-256 and hard-fails on digest mismatch
rewritten receipt whose table_sha256 or seal_sha256 no longer match — receipt is rejected, reader hashes
stale receipt whose content_addressed_chunk_sha256, chunk_count, or total_bytes disagree with the admitted manifest — receipt is rejected
does_not_cover: in-place bit flip that preserves size, mtime_ns, and inode (bit-rot or a write that restores mtime). Isolated test metadata_preserving_bitflip_is_the_residual_window documents this: admission returns the flipped bytes; HAWKING_DSV4F_VERIFY=full hard-fails.
a forged receipt written by a process that can already write the receipt file. The receipt is tamper-evident (canonical JSON seal), not secretly signed.
threat_model.never_silently_downgrades: missing, unsealed, or stale receipt does not skip hashing. A per-chunk identity miss hashes that chunk and still hard-fails on SHA-256 mismatch. Delete and truncate hard-fail. HAWKING_DSV4F_VERIFY=full restores today's hash-everything path.
threat_model.clone_view: this artifact's stream-ranges.jsonl was appended (139674 = 2 x 69837), so admit uses an APFS clone view with new inodes. The receipt records identities of the durable source files. The reader remaps a clone-view chunk to the source file when the source identity still matches, then skip-hashes that file.
